key_insight: The paper argues that superconducting quantum chip design is reaching a "SPICE moment," requiring model-driven Q-EDA and a new chip development framework built from physical device modeling upward.
engineering_relevance: It reframes quantum chip design as an end-to-end engineering workflow that links layout, simulation, fabrication, packaging, and measurement feedback for scalable quantum processors.
method: Defines a Quantum Chip Paradigm Framework centered on physical-first design rather than HDL-first abstraction.
Introduces hierarchical Q-EDA layers from Josephson junctions and resonators to logical qubits, quantum IP, and Quantum SoCs.
Emphasizes PCell-based modeling, SPICE-Q simulation, Quantum PDKs, and design-technology-measurement co-optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and architectural rather than experimental, so its support comes from system-level analysis of scaling pressures, complexity, and the need for reusable engineering objects.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is standardizing accurate device, process, and cryogenic measurement models across foundries and toolchains.
